To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The polyphosphoinositol (PI) cycle is an essential component of the signaling pathways that control cellular growth and proliferation.

the calcium-dependent phospholipase C of synaptosomes is activated by muscarinic choline receptors, that the enzyme has an apparent Km for phosphatidyl inositol 4,5-biphosphate of about 1.5 μM, and that the hydrolysis of phosphatidyl 4,5-inositol biphosphate is inhibited by lithium ions.
The calcium-activated hydrolytic activity of triphospho-inositides in synaptosomes is increased by cholinergic agonists and that this effect is blocked by atropine and scopolamine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of the phosphoinosititides in synaptosomal fractions of brain cortex and in particular with the hydrolysis of these phospholipids as a result of stimulation of the cholinergic synapse.
the role of triphosphonucleotides in the regulation of the release of transmitter substances.

the following aspects of phosphoinositide metabolism: (1) the turnover of triphospho-inositide and diphosphoinosititide in brain synaptosomes; (2) the effects of drugs on this turnover and on the release of inositol phosphates from brain synaptosomes and other tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polyphosphate inositol lipids of the brain are not involved in the mechanism of synaptic transmission.
the polyphos-phoinositides of synaptosomes are hydrolysed by a calcium-activated phospholipase C, the activity of which is increased by acetylcholine and other agents.
the turnover of triphosphatidyl inositol in the brain is very high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cholinergic stimulation causes hydrolysis of polyphosphoinositol in the plasma membrane of nerve endings and that the resulting products, inositol, inositol monophosphate, inositol bisphosphate and inositol trisphosphate, are then metabolized to inositol and glycerol phosphate.
cholinergic stimulation of brain cortex synaptosomes leads to a rapid breakdown of triphosphatidylinositols.
triphosphatidyl-inositol is the precursor of a diacylglycerolcerol which in turn is a precursor of inositol and phosphatidylinostol (Dawson, 1974; Hawthorne, 1976).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more careful about what we’re eating.
calcium is a very important regulator of phospholipid hydrolysis in synaptosomes, and that the phosphatidyserine cycle is a major source of diacylglycerol in these nerve terminals.
calcium is a critical component in the activation of phosphoinositide hydrolysis and that the hydrolytic products of phosphoinositides are important in mediating calcium mobilization.
